# Journal Themes and Publication Quality Gates

Scientific journals impose strict typographic, dimensional, and contrast guidelines on submitted figures. `cliomicplot` provides journal theme presets and an automated verification gate (`cli_scifig_qa`) enforcing submission rules.

## Journal Themes Overview

`clitheme()` implements aesthetic profiles matched to target journals:

| Preset | Journal / Style | Primary Palette | Key Typography & Grid |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `nature` | *Nature*, *Nature Medicine* | Slate Blue, Orange, Cyan | Helvetica/Arial, crisp border, no major grid |
| `science` | *Science*, *Sci Transl Med* | Jewel Navy, Crimson, Emerald | High-contrast jewel tones, clean serif/sans |
| `cell` | *Cell*, *Immunity*, *Neuron* | Obsidian Dark, Neon, Magenta | Vivid palettes, dark and light variants |
| `lancet` | *The Lancet* | Editorial Cyan, Navy, Grey | Thin strokes, minimal framing, serif title |
| `nejm` | *N Engl J Med* | Classic Crimson, Navy, Amber | Classic editorial layout, clean axes |
| `scifig` | Universal Fig4papers | Colorblind-safe palettes | Strict font floor $\ge 5.0$ pt, no stroke overlap |

```{r journal-themes-comparison, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.8}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(101)
demo_df <- data.frame(
  Biomarker = factor(rep(c("Placebo", "Biologic_Low", "Biologic_High"), each = 25)),
  Response  = c(rnorm(25, 20, 5), rnorm(25, 45, 6), rnorm(25, 78, 8))
)

p_nat <- cliplot(Response ~ Biomarker, data = demo_df, type = "boxplot", preset = "nature", title = "Nature Style")
p_lan <- cliplot(Response ~ Biomarker, data = demo_df, type = "boxplot", preset = "lancet", title = "Lancet Style")

p_nat
p_lan
```

## Journal Dimension Specifications: `cli_journal_size()`

`cli_journal_size()` calculates exact figure dimensions in millimeters and inches:

```{r journal-sizes}
# Dimensions for Nature double-column
size_nature_double <- cli_journal_size(journal = "nature", column = "double")
size_nature_double

# Dimensions for Science single-column
size_science_single <- cli_journal_size(journal = "science", column = "single")
size_science_single
```

## The AI4SciFig Quality Assurance Gate: `cli_scifig_qa()`

`cli_scifig_qa()` inspects a plot object and flags publication non-compliances:

- Text elements below the font floor ($\le 5.0$ pt).
- Missing axis labels or clipped tick marks.
- Low-contrast color pairings.
- Element clipping beyond the plot border.

```{r scifig-qa-demo}
# Run QA verification on plot
qa_report <- cli_scifig_qa(p_nat, journal = "nature", column = "double")
qa_report
```

Plots configured with `scifig = TRUE` apply these constraints automatically.
